title: Graceful shutdown uses only tokio stdlib primitives
description: The entire graceful shutdown path in both binaries — signal handling (tokio::signal::ctrl_c, tokio::signal::unix::signal), connection limiting (tokio::sync::Semaphore), channel-based drain (tokio::sync::mpsc), and timeout (tokio::time::timeout) — uses only primitives already available in tokio itself. No tokio-util, no async-shutdown, no triggered, no stop-token crate is introduced. This keeps the dependency surface minimal and avoids version pinning conflicts that are common in async Rust ecosystems. Alternative rejected: tokio_util::sync::CancellationToken, which is the most commonly recommended approach in tokio ecosystem documentation. It would require adding tokio-util as a direct dependency (it is already a transitive dependency, but pinning a direct dependency creates a version constraint). The semaphore + channel approach achieves the same result with types already in scope.
